\section{Terminal financial audit}\label{sec:financial-terminal-audit}
We instantiate 2400 long-only strategies over 25 ETFs. Development (2009--2014) fixes the library and beliefs; validation (2015--2019) fixes pruning and ranking; a SHA-256 decision record precedes locked 2020--2024 scoring. Costs are 5 basis points one way. This is a mechanism test, not a return-prediction design.

\paragraph{Results.} Frontier-only pruning preserved validation value but lowered future candidate quality by -0.0016; safe deletion compressed 80 to 25 with no registered change. Coverage ranking was adverse: top-10 improvement was -0.1560, versus -0.0685 for the best comparator. The accounting identity held, and 1 dominated policy retained positive generative value.
\paragraph{Data and claim boundary.} Licensed rows and the local ETF panel are not distributed. Aggregate artifacts are publishable; licensed reviewers reproduce them with documented CRSP extracts, while ORATS is optional for re-auditing the frozen inventory. The universe is not survivorship-free, the snapshot is not revision-timestamped, and the holdout is retrospective. The evidence concerns finite-library mechanisms and supports no market-alpha claim.
